      "endEvent": 35,
      "reason": "Opening edited montage replays fragments of later exchanges about scientific explanation, Bach, poetry, suffering, divine complexity, and speaking in tongues. E36 is the musical transition into the introduction."
    }

      "endEvent": 1807,

      "contextEndEvent": 1869,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "If this were the end of the story",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "comfort"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "A possible future beyond predation could insulate divine goodness from suffering without explaining why that suffering occurs. However, Williams offers a question and twice says he does not know (E1803–1807), accepts the objection as fair (E1745–1748), and subsequently denies providing a solution (E1823–1825). Unrestricted compensatory protection is not established."
    },

      "startEvent": 1836,
      "endEvent": 1857,
      "contextStartEvent": 1795,
      "contextEndEvent": 1869,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "destructiveness does not have the last word",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",

        "identity"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The affirmation presents redemption as prevailing over destructiveness, but the passage does not establish how Christian solidarity warrants that ultimate conclusion. Calling the issue a choice not settled purely rationally (E1844–1862) could deflect the objection; nevertheless, Williams explicitly presents a faith commitment and an added dimension, not a solution (E1823–1828, E1863–1869)."
    },

      "endEvent": 2259,

      "quote": "You you cannot be simple and do the things that that God is supposed to do.",
      "form": "yes",

      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Calling the conclusion self-evident leaves the contested bridge from complex capacities to a necessarily composite agent unestablished. Yet Dawkins supplies concrete capacities and an ordinary explanatory argument (E2118–2134, E2238–2252), so this may summarize a disputed premise rather than replace reasoning. He neither disqualifies critics nor makes contrary evidence automatically confirm his position."
    }
